_: CI-045. The names no script or workflow may spell out. Where capsules and metrics live is the registry's storage: block, read through claude-kit's dd-storage resolver; a script that names the bucket, a working-copy folder or the retired _metrics prefix is a second copy of that fact. `allow` is the only exception list: one row per file, with the reason, in the same change that adds the file. Tests and fixtures are exempt by path (see EXEMPT_PATH in lib/rules.mjs).

allow.reason: generated by tools/cloud/build_setup.py as a bundle of the kit's own files, so a finding in it is a finding in the original, which this rule reads
runs on the fleet box, where a dd-repo-registry checkout for the resolver is not guaranteed; routing it needs that checkout on the fleet first (logged as a follow-up under DOM-438)

reads the collector's Search Console archive from a Mac folder it names itself; the collector no longer keeps that folder on the Mac, so it needs the archive from the cloud state instead (DOM-438 follow-up)
writes a source label that names the old Mac folder; reword it to say where the data came from (DOM-438 follow-up)
an error message that names the old Mac folder of recipients; reword it to point at the registry storage block (DOM-438 follow-up)

the one place the literal bucket, account, capsule root and nightly excludes are written, for the workflows that load it without a registry checkout; dd_r2_env checks every value against the registry's storage block whenever prepare.sh has run (DOM-438 Phase 1b)

retired writer for the dd-work-01 box (deleted 9 November 2026): it writes the retired _metrics prefix by design, is installed on no live host and is kept only until its units are removed from the kit (DOM-438 Phase 1b)
one-off cutover record for the retired dd-main-01 box: it copies that box's archive once and runs nowhere now (DOM-438 Phase 1b)
installer for the deleted dd-work-01 box; the one line removes the working-copy folder that a hand install left there, so it names that folder to delete it (DOM-438 Phase 1b)
